How It Works

Reverse osmosis membranes like the RO membrane TW-4040-HF use a semi-permeable barrier to separate water molecules from dissolved salts and impurities. Under pressure, water is pushed across the membrane surface. Clean water (permeate) enters the central tube, while concentrated contaminants are rejected and flushed away. This process ensures safe, low-TDS water output for drinking, cooking, industrial processing, or other uses.

Because the HF (high flow) version is engineered to produce more water at a similar rejection rate, it's especially useful in systems where water demand is higher or where system efficiency matters.

Installation & Maintenance Tips

To keep your RO membrane TW-4040-HF operating well:

  1. Pre-treat feedwater with sediment and activated carbon filters to reduce chlorine and particulates.
  2. Flush new membranes at low pressure before full operation to remove preservatives.
  3. Monitor feed water pressure and TDS levels regularly to catch early signs of fouling.
  4. Replace pre-filters on schedule to protect the RO membrane and extend its lifespan.

Following these steps helps prevent premature fouling and ensures reliable water quality.

4040 RO Housing - Strong FRP Membrane Vessel

The 4040 RO housing is a durable FRP vessel designed to hold three standard 4040 reverse osmosis membranes. It works well in industrial, commercial, and large residential RO systems. Moreover, it handles pressures up to 300?PSI, keeping membranes protected from corrosion and wear.

How the RO Vessel Works

Water enters the RO housing under pressure and then flows through the membranes to separate clean water from brine. This active filtration removes impurities efficiently. Because it relies on water pressure, the system does not require electricity. Therefore, you can install it in homes, offices, factories, or laboratories without extra equipment.

Key Features

  • Rated for 300?PSI, ideal for high-pressure RO systems

Benefits of Using an RO Vessel

Installing this RO vessel increases system capacity and ensures reliable water filtration. In addition, the strong FRP material reduces the risk of leaks, keeping the system safe and efficient. Furthermore, its lightweight design simplifies installation and maintenance. Using a high-quality membrane housing extends membrane life and maintains consistent water quality.

Installation and Maintenance

Place the vessel on a stable frame, connect the inlet and outlet properly, and check O-rings and seals regularly. Also, replace the membranes as recommended. By following these steps, your RO system will continue delivering clean water consistently.

4040 Stainless Steel RO Housing – Heavy-Duty Membrane Vessel

The 4040 Stainless Steel RO Housing is a robust pressure vessel crafted from 304-grade stainless steel. It holds a standard 4? x 40? RO membrane and offers superior strength and corrosion resistance compared with plastic housings, making it ideal for demanding water purification systems.

Because this housing is built to endure up to 300 PSI,�it works well in industrial, commercial, and high-capacity residential reverse osmosis applications where durability and pressure resistance are essential. Its strong body helps protect internal components, even under continuous use.

Technical Specifications

Here are the key details for this RO membrane housing:

  • Membrane Compatibility: Standard 4? x 40? RO membranes (most brands)
  • Housing Material: 304 stainless steel for strength and rust resistance
  • Maximum Working Pressure: 300 PSI (�21 bar)
  • End Cap Material: Glass-reinforced polyimide
  • O-Ring Material: EPDM seals for secure pressure retention
  • Port Sizes: Feed and concentrate 3/4? BSP female; permeate 1/2? BSP female
  • Closure Type: U-clamp design for secure sealing and easier maintenance

This stainless steel construction delivers excellent corrosion resistance, so the housing lasts longer than many FRP or plastic housings in environments where metal contact and moisture are constant.

How It Works in RO Systems

In a reverse osmosis setup, high-pressure feed water enters the housing and moves along the membrane's surface. First, water flows through the inlet port. Then, the semi-permeable membrane separates to produce purified water (permeate), which exits through the centre outlet, while reject water leaves via the side port. Therefore, the housing supports effective water purification with minimal leaks and stable performance.

Benefits of Stainless Steel Construction

Using a stainless steel RO vessel offers several advantages:

  • Long Life: Stands up to corrosion better than non-metal housings.
  • Pressure Reliability: Designed for high-pressure operation with stable performance.
  • Easy Maintenance: The U-clamp design allows quicker membrane changes.
  • Wide Use: Suitable for factories, labs, food & beverage plants, and large home setups.

Installation Tips

Mount the housing on a stable frame, and always use proper thread sealant on BSP fittings to prevent leaks. Also, check the EPDM O-rings regularly and replace them if worn, to keep the system tight and effective.
